First, I started working at Walmart for the summer about a month ago. One of my co-workers is a female in her early to mid-30s, physically in good shape, and as far as I can tell, she doesn't have any physical disabilities. I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she responded, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I replied, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." She then said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team (not my boss, just the most senior person who directs us) walked up to me and said he just spoke to her. He told me that the next time someone asks for help, I need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you would like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." Feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's two against one, with the co-worker and the head guy against me. Let me break this down. She got upset and left. Then the head guy told me I should help her, and I pushed back, saying we're both paid to do the same job and she should be able to do it. I also mentioned HR. However, there's also the aspect of fairness and not overstepping one's responsibilities. So, was I wrong to refuse to lift the box alone? Or was I right to stand my ground because it's part of my job and I shouldn't have to do all the work? I think the key points are: 1. That seems fair because both of us are paid to do the same job. 4. The head guy told me I should help her, but I clarified the situation and stood my ground, suggesting HR if needed. From an Islamic perspective, helping others is a good deed, but it's also important to maintain fairness and not take on responsibilities that aren't yours.
